summary: Ledger-first: the hash-chained JSONL ledger is the only source of truth; decisions, constraints and questions are projected into a rebuildable SQLite index. Graphiti is optional asynchronous enrichment, never on the write path.

record.text: Ledger-first: the hash-chained JSONL ledger is the only source of truth; decisions, constraints and questions are projected into a rebuildable SQLite index. Graphiti is optional asynchronous enrichment, never on the write path.
record.rationale: Verified 2026-10-21: the LLM gateway has no embeddings endpoint, GLM 5.3 always reasons (6-12s/call, so ~1-2 min per Graphiti write), and LLM extraction turns structured decisions into lossy entity-fact triples with non-deterministic supersession. Lenses already write structured records, so store them as such.

summary: A record supersedes another only by naming its id, and only if that record is active (otherwise the error names the current one). Policy outcomes are stored in the event so replay is faithful.

summary: Lens identity is not actually fixed: _actor() prefers the tool's `actor` argument over NAZARETH_ACTOR, and every write tool still exposes `actor` (decide's docstring even invites "`actor` is who you are"). A lens can pass actor="human" and bypass the human-ownership rule. Reproduced: with NAZARETH_ACTOR=lens:code, decide(..., actor="human", supersedes=[<human decision>]) returns status "active" and the ledger records actor "human". This undercuts dec-f753fa (fixed NAZARETH_ACTOR per lens) and dec-12725e (lens superseding a human decision must be pending); the lens templates only say "never pass actor" in the prompt. A misbehaving or prompt-injected lens could silently overturn human decisions and forge audit-trail authorship.

render_context budgets only decisions; constraints (and recent answers) are unbounded and come first, then the whole text is hard-cut at 9000 chars. Reproduced with 40 x 300-char constraints: output is 9000 chars ending mid-constraint, with no "Active decisions" block, no "Waiting on the human ... Don't rely on pending decisions" warning, and no tail instructions. The session-start agent then sees no pending-review warning and no hint that the snapshot was truncated.

install() is not robust to existing config it doesn't expect. Invalid JSON in .mcp.json or .claude/settings.json raises a raw JSONDecodeError traceback after .nazareth/ and the lens files were already written (partial install, no actionable message). A non-dict mcpServers or a SessionStart group that isn't a dict raises AttributeError/TypeError the same way. Writes are not atomic, so an interrupt mid-write can truncate the user's settings.json. Existing valid entries are correctly preserved (covered by tests).

The dogfooding setup is not committed: .claude/agents/*, .claude/settings.json and .mcp.json are untracked, even though commit b7df4fb says "start dogfooding nazareth" and the ledger is committed (dec-97b81a). A fresh clone gets the ledger but no lenses, MCP registration or context hook. Also .claude/settings.local.json is a per-user file and isn't in .gitignore, so a blanket `git add .claude` would commit it. The installed agent files are byte-identical to the templates.

The hook command ("nazareth context"), the .mcp.json server and all three lens servers call a bare `nazareth` that must be on PATH. When nazareth is installed only in a project .venv and Claude Code is started without activating it, every SessionStart shows a hook error and the lens subagents start with no lens-memory tools. That breaks the memory protocol quietly: the main session's nazareth tools are denied to the lenses (dec-f753fa), so they have no memory access at all. A corrupt ledger likewise makes `nazareth context` print a traceback on every session start.
test entry: lens actor can be spoofed via actor argument

When called from this lens session, every lens-memory `log` call returned the generic "Error executing tool log", yet each event was appended to the ledger and indexed (evt_73e175aa..., evt_a29b58cd..., evt_4ca90cef..., evt_e1021ccd..., evt_9a1c2abf...; plus a probe evt_275621bc... that I logged while diagnosing). The same call succeeds both in-process and over a raw stdio MCP client against the same editable install, so the cause sits between the Claude Code subagent host and the inline server and is still unknown. Consequence: a lens believes its write failed and retries, producing duplicate ledger entries (this already happened once here), or it reports work as unrecorded when it was in fact recorded.

summary: Implemented dec-bdedaf: _actor() now prefers a non-empty NAZARETH_ACTOR over the per-call argument and raises NazarethError if either one is "human" (after strip and lower-case), pointing the caller to the `nazareth` CLI. The decide docstring now says `actor` is used only when the server has no fixed identity. Fixes evt_73e175aa7aaa4080. Lens templates already say "never pass actor", so they are unchanged.

Added actor-trust tests: env actor beats argument, argument used without env, human rejected via argument (3 casings) and via env, and the original repro (lens env + actor="human" superseding a human decision) now errors and the human decision stays active. An autouse fixture clears NAZARETH_ACTOR. test_phase_read_and_set no longer passes actor="human". 66 passed, ruff clean.

Lens write errors (evt_cfa95602) fixed. Cause: the MCP SDK runs sync tools on worker threads; parallel calls from one lens hit the shared SQLite connection from a thread other than its creator (sqlite3.ProgrammingError). log appended to the ledger before crashing in index.sync(), so it landed but reported an error; ask syncs first, so it was lost. Fix: server.call() serializes tool calls per process with a lock; Projection opens SQLite with check_same_thread=False. Regression test: test_parallel_calls_on_one_server. Running servers need a restart to pick it up.

Actor-trust (dec-bdedaf) can be bypassed through the CLI. All three lens templates grant Bash (lens-code inherits every tool), and the `nazareth` CLI records every write as actor "human" with no check, even when NAZARETH_ACTOR is set. Verified in a scratch project: `NAZARETH_ACTOR=lens:code nazareth decide storage SQLite --why x` returned status "active" and history shows actor "human". So a misbehaving or prompt-injected lens can still answer questions, resolve pending items, supersede human decisions and forge human authorship by running `nazareth decide/answer/resolve` from Bash, getting around the MCP-side rejection and the pending gate (dec-12725e). Possible mitigations: have the CLI refuse writes when NAZARETH_ACTOR is set (that only stops casual misuse, since a lens can unset the variable), and/or add Bash deny rules for `nazareth` write subcommands to the lens templates. This doesn't block an MVP merge, but the trust model is weaker than dec-bdedaf says.

Should lenses be prevented from writing as "human" through the `nazareth` CLI via Bash (finding evt_97e920f6bf824a0d), and if so how: CLI refuses writes when NAZARETH_ACTOR is set, Bash deny rules in lens templates, both, or accept the risk for MVP?

Verified: with NAZARETH_ACTOR=lens:code, `nazareth decide ...` lands as an active human decision. An env check is easy to get around (a lens can unset the variable). Claude Code permission deny rules such as Bash(nazareth decide:*) are stronger but host-specific.

Analysis for q-0bfe36, deferred. "CLI refuses writes when NAZARETH_ACTOR is set" does nothing on its own: NAZARETH_ACTOR is set only in each lens's MCP server env, not in the Bash shells that agents get. Making it work needs an `env` block in .claude/settings.json. That affects only Claude Code sessions in projects that have it, but it also blocks the human's `!` commands, and any agent can get around it with `env -u`. Rejected for now because the cost is high and it only catches honest mistakes. A real fix needs a signal the agent can't fake, for example a Touch ID / keychain or interactive-TTY confirmation on human CLI writes. Brainstorm that before dogfooding on Firefly.

record.text: Semantic search is an optional `nazareth[search]` extra using model2vec (potion-base-8M) behind a pluggable embedder interface. Vectors live in .nazareth/vectors.db (gitignored, derived, reset by `rebuild`). Records missing vectors are embedded lazily at query time, outside ledger.transaction(); `nazareth embed` warms the store. `query` ranks with hybrid FTS5 + vector reciprocal rank fusion, and falls back to FTS5 alone when the extra isn't installed.
record.rationale: model2vec needs only numpy, ~30 MB, microsecond embeddings, good on short text. Lazy query-time embedding keeps the write path untouched (dec-f9e534) with no daemon or staleness. Optional extra keeps the core dependency-light; the install script will install it. Needle was considered and rejected: its text-embedding API is undocumented, it downloads a native engine, and telemetry is on by default. Approved by the human in chat 2026-10-21.

summary: accepted dec-0b83d2

Implemented dec-f7ed65 semantic search: Embedder protocol, Model2VecEmbedder (potion-base-8M; loads from HF cache with local_files_only first, downloads only if missing), VectorStore over .nazareth/vectors.db (id, kind, embedder, text hash, float32), lazy sync at query time from the FTS corpus (Projection.documents), hybrid FTS5 + cosine top-50 with RRF k=60 in Memory.search. Vector-only hits below cosine 0.3 are dropped. Any embedder failure turns vectors off for the process and falls back to FTS; the CLI notes it once on stderr. The write path's related_active stays FTS-only. `nazareth embed` added; `rebuild` deletes vectors.db; init now backfills missing .gitignore patterns (vectors.db*). Install with the `search` extra (model2vec>=0.4,<1, numpy); dev includes it.

Added tests/test_vectors.py (13 tests, deterministic synonym-aware hashed-BoW fake embedder in tests/conftest.py; autouse fixture keeps every other test keyword-only and off the network). pytest: 90 passed; ruff: clean. Real smoke test on this repo: `nazareth embed` downloaded the model in about 3 s and embedded 34 items. "where do lenses get their identity" moved dec-f753fa from FTS rank 5 to hybrid rank 2, and dec-bdedaf from 6 to 5. A nonsense query's best cosine was 0.16, below the 0.3 cutoff.

The first `query` in a server process whose model isn't cached yet downloads potion-base-8M (vectors.py:79) while holding the server's process-wide call lock (server.py:57). Every other tool call in that lens, writes included (decide/constrain/ask/log/phase), waits until the download finishes or fails. On a slow or stalled network a write can hit the MCP client timeout. No write calls the network itself, so dec-f9e534 is respected as written, but its intent (writes never depend on the network) is not. Possible fixes: do the model load/download outside the lock, or never download from the MCP/query path and leave downloading to `nazareth embed`. Not verified live because the model is already cached here; found by reading the code.

Projects initialized before this change only get the `vectors.db*` gitignore pattern if the human re-runs `nazareth init`, and neither the README nor the CLI says to. vectors.db is created on the first query in any initialized project once the search extra is installed. It then shows up as untracked (plus -wal/-shm), and `git add .nazareth` would commit a binary derived file. This drifts from dec-93ceaf ("derived files are gitignored inside it"). This repo's own .nazareth/.gitignore was fixed by hand. Possible fixes: a README/upgrade note, a one-line hint when vectors.db is first created and the pattern is missing, or creating vectors.db only from `nazareth embed`/`init`.

`_semantic` catches every Exception and sets `vector_error` for the life of the process. A transient failure therefore switches off semantic search in a long-lived lens server until the Claude session restarts. Examples: SQLite "database is locked" after the 30 s busy timeout, being offline at the first query, a momentary hub error. Agents get no signal (MCP `query` doesn't expose `vector_error`), so a lens can't tell it is getting keyword-only results. Search keeps working and nothing errors, which matches the requirement. Consider disabling permanently only on EmbedderUnavailable and retrying other errors, or adding a `semantic: false` hint to the query result.

`VectorStore.reset()` (used by `nazareth rebuild`) unlinks vectors.db, -wal and -shm while other `nazareth serve` processes may hold them open. Those processes keep reading and writing the orphaned inode until they restart: wasted re-embedding and disk held, though results stay correct because sync hashes against the index. Verified: 6 search/log processes plus 8 overlapping rebuilds finished without errors and integrity_check was ok, but the per-process counts diverged (668 to 1026 against 1026 docs in the live file), which confirms the orphaning. There is also an unverified narrow race: a process opening the new file between the unlink of the main file and the unlink of -wal/-shm could have its fresh WAL deleted. Separately, sync computes `gone` from a docs snapshot taken before it reads `stored`, so a process with an older index can delete vectors another process just added. That self-heals on the next search. All of this is derived and self-healing; it doesn't block the merge. A safer reset is DELETE FROM vectors plus clearing meta inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE instead of unlinking.

Test gaps. (1) conftest.py imports numpy at module level, and test_vectors imports huggingface_hub, so without the search extra the whole suite fails at collection; the "falls back to FTS without the extra" path is never tested in a real core-only environment. Use pytest.importorskip. (2) The real Model2VecEmbedder's 0.3 cutoff and the local_files_only to download fallback order are untested. The fake uses min_similarity 0.2, and the load-failure test patches snapshot_download to fail both calls, so it never checks that a cached model loads without the network. (3) There is no multi-process test of vectors.db. Otherwise the tests check real behaviour, not the fake: write tools never embed, lazy pickup, inactive filtering, limit, embedder-change wipe, rebuild reset, CLI fallback note. They are network-free: the autouse fixture forces default_embedder to None, and the one Model2VecEmbedder test fails both download calls.
